notes:
Summary: Stellaris is evaluating Redwood Dedicated with the goal of replacing an internal, self-hosted inference fleet. Primary driver: consistent latency (support chat + regret-reduction reranking) and strong auditability for regulated customers. They have a mix of streaming chat (agent UI) and non-streaming batch reranking for nightly pipelines. Key asks: clear definitions for p50/p95/p99, authoritative measurement method, and reserved GPU planning that maps to throughput guarantees.

Important quotes / paraphrases: "We need p95 < 200ms for agent messages to feel real-time; occasional p99 spikes acceptable but must be visible in alerts" — Head of Product.

Latency SLO alignment items discussed:
- Measurement boundary: customer insists on end-to-end (client-side) numbers for UX acceptance; Redwood will provide server-side (edge + serving) percentiles. Need reconciliation method (see "reconciliation proposal" below).
- Percentile semantics: agreed baseline definitions — p50 median, p95 95th sample percentile per-minute window, p99 99th; define sample population as successful generation requests only (exclude 5xx).
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming (token-by-token) measured as time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-to-last-token (TTLT) for long responses. Non-streaming measured as total server processing time. Proposal: provide both TTFT p95 and TTLT p95 for streaming routes.
- Client-side timing caveats: network jitter, SDK batching, and browser rendering cause variance. Proposed approach: Redwood SDK will emit client-side trace id and attach server-side timestamps so customer can compute end-to-end; Redwood will publish server-side percentiles and a reconcile report showing median delta between client and server timings during test windows.
- Measurement windows & sampling: 5-minute rolling windows for SLO evaluation, 72-hour historical retention for SLA dispu tes, synthetic canary every 15s per-region for external validation.

Throughput / reserved GPU planning notes:
- Baseline asks: sustained 400 QPS (short chat messages), burst 1200 QPS for peak events, batch reranking throughput target 50K items/hour.
- Redwood proposed dedicated pool sizing: 8x A100-equivalent partitions (estimate) with autoscale headroom + burst nodes. Customer asks explicit token/sec and sustained concurrency numbers per reserved GPU for contract.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit to 12-month reserved contract if latency SLOs + legal terms acceptable.

SLA negotiation points to resolve:
1) Which side is authoritative for SLA breaches (server-only or client-end-to-end)? Stellaris prefers client-end-to-end but accepts server-side for billing/credits, with reconciliation logs.
2) Credits formula: propose tiered credits based on p95 and p99 miss windows; Stellaris requests at least two remediation options: credits or prioritized capacity (fast reprovision).
3) Measurement transparency: Redwood to provide access to telemetry dashboards for joint incident reviews and to share raw percentile exports for independent verification quarterly.

Next technical steps agreed:
- Redwood to deliver revised SLA language that explicitly defines measurement boundaries, percentile calc method (per-minute aggregation then global percentile), and streaming metrics (TTFT/TTLT) — due 2026-03-18.
- SE to run a joint synthetic load test (staging) with Stellaris test harness to produce matched client/server traces (target week of 2026-03-22).
- Architect note: include KV cache warming plan for burst events and explicit token budget per-request to forecast GPU utilization.

Links / artifacts: referenced capacity_plan.xlsx and slo-proposal-v2.pdf in Drive; see Fireflies ff-20260302-8812 for demo transcript.
